steps.body: You can tell if a fraction is more or less than 1/2 without ever finding a common denominator. Just compare the numerator to **half the denominator.** For 5/8: half of 8 is 4, and 5 is more than 4 — so 5/8 is more than 1/2.

widget.prompt: Sort each fraction: is it more than 1/2, less than 1/2, or exactly 1/2?

items.feedback: Half of 10 is 5, and 7 is more than 5 — more than 1/2.
Half of 10 is 5, and 4 is less than 5 — less than 1/2.
Half of 3 is 1.5, and 2 is more than that — more than 1/2.

widget.missFeedback: Compare the numerator to HALF the denominator — bigger, smaller, or exactly equal.
widget.successFeedback: 7/10 and 2/3 beat their halfway mark; 4/10 falls short; 5/10 lands exactly on it.

options.label: Its top is more than half its bottom

predict.reveal: Half of the denominator is the tipping point — 5/8 clears it because 5 beats 4. The benchmark lives in that comparison, no drawing required.

explanationVariants: Half of 3 is 1.5, and 1 is less than 1.5 — so 1/3 is less than 1/2.

widget.prompt: Is 1/3 more than, less than, or exactly 1/2?
widget.eqFeedback: Exactly half of 3 would need a numerator of 1.5, which isn't a whole number here. 1/3 is less than 1/2.
widget.gtFeedback: Half of 3 is 1.5, and 1 is LESS than 1.5 — 1/3 falls short of 1/2, not past it.
widget.successFeedback: Half of 3 is 1.5; 1 is smaller than that, so 1/3 falls short of 1/2.

steps.body: Odd denominators make 'half the denominator' a decimal — annoying. Here's a cleaner version: **double the numerator, then compare it to the denominator.** For 2/3: double 2 to get 4; compare 4 to 3. Since 4 > 3, the fraction is more than 1/2. Same answer, no decimals.

explanationVariants: Double the numerator: 3 × 2 = 6. Compare to the denominator, 8: 6 is less than 8, so 3/8 is less than 1/2.
6 < 8, so 3/8 falls short of the halfway mark.

widget.prompt: Using the doubling trick, is 3/8 more than, less than, or exactly 1/2?
widget.eqFeedback: An even denominator alone doesn't guarantee exactly half. Doubling the numerator (6) and comparing to 8 shows 3/8 is less than 1/2.
widget.gtFeedback: The size of 3 alone doesn't decide it. Doubled, 3 becomes 6, which is LESS than the denominator 8 — so 3/8 is less than 1/2.
widget.successFeedback: 3 doubled is 6, and 6 is smaller than 8 — 3/8 falls short of 1/2.

widget.missFeedback: Double the numerator, then compare it to the denominator: bigger, smaller, or exactly equal.
widget.successFeedback: 5/8 and 7/13 beat their halfway mark; 4/9 falls short; 6/12 lands exactly on it.

explanationVariants: Double the numerator: 11 × 2 = 22. Compare to 20: 22 is more than 20, so 11/20 is more than 1/2.

widget.prompt: Is 11/20 more than, less than, or exactly 1/2?
widget.ltFeedback: Barely still counts. 11 doubled is 22, which beats 20 — so 11/20 IS more than 1/2, just by a little.
widget.eqFeedback: A round denominator doesn't guarantee exactly half. Doubling 11 gives 22, which is more than 20, not equal to it.
widget.successFeedback: 11 doubled is 22, and 22 is more than 20 — 11/20 clears the halfway mark.

explanationVariants: Doubled, 13 becomes 26. Since 26 is more than 24, 13/24 is more than 1/2 — the survey favors summer.
26 > 24, so more than half the people prefer summer.

widget.prompt: A survey shows 13 out of 24 people prefer summer. Is that more or less than half?
widget.ltFeedback: Being close to 12 doesn't settle it. Doubling 13 gives 26, which beats 24 — so it IS more than half.
widget.eqFeedback: Exactly half of 24 would be 12 people, not 13. Since 13 is one more than that, it's more than half — confirmed by 13×2=26>24.
widget.successFeedback: 13 doubled is 26, which is more than 24 — just over half prefer summer.

takeaways: A fraction is more than 1/2 when the numerator beats half the denominator.
The doubling trick avoids decimals: double the numerator, compare to the denominator.
This works with any denominator, odd or even, without ever finding a common one.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Double the numerator, compare it to the denominator.** For 3/5: double 3 to get 6. Compare 6 to 5: 6 is more than 5, so 3/5 is more than 1/2.
